body.instructions:
@@MANUAL@@

## Base backgrounds (기준 배경)
Sometimes the app sends base backgrounds instead of reference images: finished backgrounds of this same place that our team already made for this episode, each with a short Korean note (for example "소파 쪽"). They are Images 2 to k+1. Image 1 is then a new rough of the same place from another camera: a slightly turned view, another wall of the room, or a closer shot. The new picture must clearly be the same place, as if the same set were filmed from the new camera.
- Image 1 decides the camera, the layout and what is in the picture. Never copy the composition or the camera of a base background.
- Find every object and surface of Image 1 in the base backgrounds and describe it as it looks there: its colors, its shape and two to four key features, and the number of the image that shows it (for example "the wine-red tufted sofa with gold claw feet, as in image 2"). A loose or unclear shape in Image 1 where a base background has an object is that object.
- Name the walls, the floor, the baseboard, the ceiling, the windows and the doors as they look in the base backgrounds, also when Image 1 shows a side of the room that no base background shows: that side keeps the same wallpaper, floor, baseboard, window frames and doors. Objects there that no base background shows are drawn as Image 1 shows them, in the same plain look as the furniture of the base backgrounds.
- Keep the sizes: a sofa or a door is as big compared to the room as in the base backgrounds.
- Never add an object from a base background where Image 1 shows none.
- Write the marker [SAME PLACE] right after the layout rule (item 5); the app replaces it with the team's sentence about the base backgrounds. Item 6 is for reference images only: do not write it for base backgrounds.
- The base backgrounds already show our style for this place, so the app sends no style examples: style_picks must be [] and item 8 is left out.

## Painted rough
The artist painted Image 1 with the flat colors of this place. The painted walls, floor and ceiling and the painted window and door openings are the exact room: keep exactly where the floor meets the walls (the floor line and its slope), the corners of the walls and the ceiling, and the position and size of every window and door opening. In the layout, say where these borders run in plain words (for example "the floor line runs from the bottom left up to the right").
- Furniture and other objects, whether painted or drawn only as pencil lines over the room, show only where each object stands, how big it is and how it is turned (for example a sofa seen at an angle). Describe each one at that place, size and angle, but with its real design, shape and proportions from image 2. The rough outline of an object in the sketch is not its shape: never copy it.
- A painted window or door opening holds a complete window or door like the ones of image 2, with its frame along every edge of the opening.
- These colors are the colors of the place: this wins over the color hint rule, so do not make them clearer or more saturated.

Image 2 is a finished background of this same place that our team already drew for this episode. This picture shows the same place from the new camera of image 1: every wall, floor, ceiling, window, door and piece of furniture that image 2 shows keeps exactly the same colors, shapes, materials and details. Only the camera changes: follow image 1 for the camera, the layout and the positions, and never copy the composition of image 2. The furniture and objects of image 1 only mark their place, size and angle: draw each one there with its real design, shape and proportions from image 2, never with the rough outline of the sketch. Image 3 shows the target drawing style: a quick freehand brush drawing, like the distant buildings, the white balcony railings, the windows and the trees in image 3. Flat colors with hard edges, clear and fairly saturated, never greyish or washed out; shapes slightly deformed by hand, lines that are not ruler-straight, rectangles a little uneven, thin things like pipes, railings and window bars drawn as single loose brush strokes, almost like a doodle. It must not look wavy or warped. Flat cel shading, no gradients, no glow, no texture, no black outlines. Time: daytime. The interior is lit with even, neutral light and keeps clear, bright, fairly saturated everyday colors; through the windows and doors you see the outside in flat daylight colors. Text: no text. Avoid: sketch lines, labels or handwriting from image 1, ruler-straight vector lines, perfect geometry, wavy distortion, fisheye distortion, black outlines, photorealism, glossy highlights, gradients, soft airbrush, glow, light falloff, light rays, painterly texture, dull greyish or washed-out colors, the playground objects of image 3, people. Aspect ratio 3:2.

## Fixed sentences for the markers
There is no app between you and the picture here: write these sentences out in full where the markers go.
[STYLE] = Image {BASE} shows the target drawing style: a quick freehand brush drawing, like the distant buildings, the white balcony railings, the windows and the trees in image {BASE}. Flat colors with hard edges, clear and fairly saturated, never greyish or washed out; shapes slightly deformed by hand, lines that are not ruler-straight, rectangles a little uneven, thin things like pipes, railings and window bars drawn as single loose brush strokes, almost like a doodle. It must not look wavy or warped. Flat cel shading, no gradients, no glow, no texture, no black outlines.
[TREES] = Trees: each tree's leaves are one to three big solid masses with a simple bumpy outline, in two flat greens with the lighter one on top, like the trees in image {BASE}, not a pattern of many small leaf clusters; a brown trunk with a few thick, loose branch strokes; every tree a little different. Bushes and hedges are low rounded mounds.
[CARS] = Cars: simple flat everyday cars of mixed types in clear body colors, with flat dark windows, small flat lights, blank plates and plain dark wheels, no shine or logos. Every car stands on its wheels with a small flat contact shadow; cars farther back are smaller and higher in the picture, never half hidden behind a hedge as if sunk.
[CARS EYE LEVEL] = the [CARS] sentence, then: At eye level, the roofs of cars near and far stay close to the horizon line.
[BUILDINGS] = Large buildings: drawn by hand like the distant buildings in image {BASE}, a few broad flat shapes slightly deformed like a quick doodle: roof lines and long edges a little tilted or bent, corners not quite square, windows a few uneven flat rectangles; never ruler-straight edges or perfectly even rows of windows.
[TIME] = Time: a clear day. Use a bright, clear daytime palette with fairly strong saturation: clean white and light cream walls, a clear saturated sky blue with a few flat-bottomed white clouds, fresh leaf greens, neutral white balance. Cast shadows are flat, slightly darker shapes. Lamps are off.
[TIME exterior] = Time: a clear day. Use a bright, clear daytime palette with fairly strong saturation: clean white and light cream walls, a clear saturated sky blue with a few flat-bottomed white clouds, fresh leaf greens, neutral white balance. Cast shadows are flat, slightly darker shapes. Lamps are off.
[TIME interior] = Time: daytime. The interior is lit with even, neutral light and keeps clear, bright, fairly saturated everyday colors; through the windows and doors you see the outside in flat daylight colors.
[LIGHT FLAT] = Light: completely flat and even with no direction; no shadows of any kind, not even small contact shadows under objects.
[LIGHT EVEN] = Light: even and neutral with no direction; no sunbeams, no light patches on the floor or walls, no strong shadows, only small flat contact shadows under objects.
[AVOID] = Avoid: sketch lines, labels or handwriting from image 1, ruler-straight vector lines, perfect geometry, wavy distortion, fisheye distortion, black outlines, photorealism, glossy highlights, gradients, soft airbrush, glow, light falloff, light rays, painterly texture, dull greyish or washed-out colors, the playground objects of image {BASE}, people. Before "people", add: the objects, layout or text of the style examples (only with style examples); identical repeated trees, many small leaf clusters (with trees); cars sunk into the ground (with cars); and your scene items.
[SAME PLACE] = Image 2 is a finished background of this same place that our team already drew for this episode.
